PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Planning Commission on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council or Planning Commission from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears
on a posted agenda. Upon request, the City Council or Planning Commission may, in their discretion, allow citizen
participation on a specific item on the agenda at the time the item is considered by the City Council and Planning
Commission. If you wish to address the City Council or planning at this time, please complete a speaker's card
and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

1.  Housing Element Workshop

  Element Update Workshop and simultaneously conduct public outreach.

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
City Councilmembers: Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo
Absent: Mayor Rebollo

Planning Commissioners: Commissioners Grajeda, Barragan, Gutierrez and Chair Gonzalez

CALL TO ORDER Vice Mayor Argumedo open Special Joint Meeting of the City Council and Planning Commission at 6:08 p.m.

ROLL CALL City Councilmembers: Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo
Absent: Mayor Rebollo

Planning Commissioners: Commissioners Grajeda, Barragan, Gutierrez and Chair Gonzalez
Commissioner Barragan arrived at 6:21 p.m.

PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the agenda or within their jurisdiction.  




SCHEDULED MATTERS

1.. Housing Element Workshop Acting Director of Economic Development & Planning Viviana Esparza presented consultant Lisa Brownfield to discuss & moderate the Housing Element Workshop via Zoom.
Information gathered from past focus groups was presented that highlighted different housing interests and needs throughout the City. Presentation called attention to possible constraints, and needed resources in order to implement an effective plan of action; it further discussed the need for locating suitable sites. 

Brief discussion ensued in reference to the City’s compliance with the number of units required and if the completed Rosewood Village project, Modelo project as well as the City’s other housing plans will satisfy the requirements under all income categories.  Consultant Veronica advised that the State will be satisfied with the current plans but work is yet to be done to meet the established  low and moderate income category. 

Resident Maria stated she is happy that the City is looking into various housing options and mentioned that she is aware the County of Los Angeles has rent control; she urged Council to allow more income housing. 
City Manager briefly mentioned the City’s current Rent Subsidy programs for seniors and shared that the City is evaluating renter and homebuyer subsidies for the public in the future. City Manager Tapia also advised that the City adopted the Rent Control statute that allows the City to prosecute violators as a Code Enforcement matter; members of the public can report a rent increase that is not within the legal permitted ranges. 

Resident Ericka B spoke in support of affordable housing, rent control and stated it is important to consider the location so it does not impact health.
Jazmin from Eastyard Communities for Environmental Justice expressed concern for the lack of rent control and stated it is important to focus on extremely low rents so families have a place to live while landlords continue raising prices.
Joe Chaidez suggested the Council explore existing homes and lots that may have the ability for additional capacity.   

Consultant proceeded to document suggestions from City Council, Planning Commissioners and the Public in reference to the major Housing issues in the City, possible challenges that may exist in the City, potential sites, use of current structures/buildings and potential sites. 

Councilmembers commented and shared some challenges they consider may exist in the City as well as ideas for possible locations. Councilmembers pointed out there may be a need for remediation and cleanup of various sites that may pose a challenge but offered various locations that can be considered such as locations off Eastern Avenue between Jillson Street and Harbor Boulevard, the Old Dairy site and various hotels off Atlantic Boulevard.  

Commissioners expressed their opinion regarding the need for affordable housing for seniors, zoning challenges as well as the need to offer incentives for developers and suggested the City look at the possibility of re-purposing underperforming company buildings and re-zone them as mixed use specifically along Washington Blvd, Eastern Ave and Atlantic Blvd. They suggested the City be creative in looking at buildings like the Alta-Med parking structure that can offer mixed uses and change zoning regulations that may allow developers the ability to design their buildings that can be adapted to various uses in the future.  
Consultant Brownfield finalized her presentation and provided a timeline; she stressed the importance of Community feedback and urged the City Council and Planning Commissioners to encourage the public to participate.  


ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:58 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
